items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: And there was a reporter, her name was Inez (Timmy) Cavanaugh, she married a baron whose name was Baron Rosen-cratz (phonetic).

ctx.x: This is February 2nd, 1979, 65 Second Avenue, Jacques Butler's home. Now, you've told me that -- before we talk about your going back to Europe after World War II -- you mentioned that you worked with Art (Hodes?) and a lot of so-called Dixieland bands, but you had also told me that on occasion before, that you had used Bud Powell at one time on your bands.

Yeah, I used Bud Powell. You see, there was -- Billy Lewis and all of us, we were ex-compatriots, we had come back from Europe, so we always hung together. And there was a reporter, her name was Inez (Timmy) Cavanaugh, she married a baron whose name was Baron Rosen-cratz (phonetic). And Baron Rosencratz had very little, very sharp bar, or something, just for his pleasure, and we always hung out there because we always talking.
